detail.longDescription: In Rust, you can use a short form to declare arrays, for example: let array: [i32; 3] = [0; 3]; Can I implement a custom short-form syntax for my own struct, which has a lot in common with hashmaps and a key/value structure? Specifically, I want this: let my_var: MyStruct = [1 => "Value1"; 2 => "Value2"]; to be a short form for a series of my_var.add(key, value.to_string()) calls. I want to do this without relying on a macro if at all possible so values can be pulled at runtime instead of compile time). (This is a follow-up to my previous question here, where I was recommended to make a more specific question.)
